intro.title: Olist Customer Satisfaction Analysis
intro.description: Analysed 99,224 customer reviews alongside order, delivery, product and seller data to identify patterns behind low satisfaction on the Olist marketplace.

image.alt: Olist customer satisfaction Power BI dashboard

description: The project investigated factors associated with low customer satisfaction on the Olist e-commerce marketplace. Customer review scores were used as a proxy for satisfaction, with 1–2 stars treated as low satisfaction, 3 stars as neutral or mixed satisfaction, and 4–5 stars as higher satisfaction.

The objective was to analyse 99,224 customer reviews alongside order, delivery, product category and seller data to identify patterns and prioritise areas for further investigation. The project scope and supporting business questions were established before any analysis took place.
Outcome: a defined business problem, objectives, scope and analytical questions.

image.alt: Business problem and project scope for the Olist analysis

stakeholders.panelTagline: Stakeholders were identified through business-context analysis. No interviews or workshops were conducted, as this was an independent portfolio project.

points.text: Customers: the source of the review scores used as a proxy for satisfaction.
Sellers: require fair and consistent comparisons of low-review proportions.
Olist management: needs evidence to prioritise areas for investigation.
Delivery partners: relevant to delivery performance and its relationship with review scores.
Customer support team: interested in monitoring customer feedback.
Requirements and outputs: low-review comparisons across sellers, categories and delivery performance; stakeholder analysis, user stories, acceptance criteria and MoSCoW prioritisation.

comparison.heading: Data Analysis & Solution Design
comparison.tagline: From examining the available data and its gaps to translating requirements into analytical comparisons and a dashboard.

image.alt: Olist datasets examined during data analysis and gap assessment

old.heading: Data Analysis & Gap Analysis
points: Five datasets examined: Order Reviews, Orders, Order Items, Products and Sellers.
Structures, key fields, data types and relationships were reviewed.
Quality issues found: missing review text, repeated review IDs and multiple reviews per order.
Further issues: missing delivery timestamps and product categories, and inconsistent dates.
Relationships were mapped to set counting methods and avoid double-counting orders or reviews.
Covers data quality and analytical gaps, not a formal AS-IS/TO-BE process map.

image.alt: Power BI customer satisfaction dashboard built during solution design

new.heading: Requirements Analysis & Solution Design
points: Requirements became comparisons of reviews, sellers, categories and delivery performance.
Rule set: 1–2 star reviews are classed as low satisfaction.
Delivery comparisons restricted to eligible orders with valid timestamps.
Counting units defined for orders, sellers and product categories.
Power Query prepared the five datasets, and Power BI presented the analysis.
Outcome: prepared datasets, defined analytical rules and a Power BI dashboard.

comparison.sliderLabel: Compare the data analysis and gap assessment with the solution design

points.title: Overall Satisfaction
points.text: 14.69% of 99,224 reviews were rated 1–2 stars, with an average review score of 4.09 out of 5.

points.title: Delivery Performance
points.text: Low-review proportion was 62.35% for late deliveries versus 9.17% on time or early: an association, not proven causation.

points.title: Seller Performance
points.text: Low-review proportions varied between the sellers examined.

points.title: Product Categories
points.text: Low-review proportions also varied across the product categories examined.

points.title: Data Quality
points.text: Missing values, repeated review IDs and timestamp inconsistencies limit analytical reliability.

points.title: Recommendations
points.text: Investigate recurring late deliveries, monitor sellers, categories and feedback consistently, and strengthen data quality and reporting definitions.

points.title: Documented Findings
points.text: Findings, recommendations and limitations were documented to support interpretation of the results.

points.title: Baseline Measures
points.text: Baselines set: overall low-review proportion, average review score and the late versus on-time gap.

points.title: Future Monitoring
points.text: Delivery performance and low-review proportions could be tracked over time to assess improvement.

points.title: Requirements Validation
points.text: Future work could check solutions against documented requirements and agreed performance indicators.

points.title: Testing Support
points.text: Functional and user acceptance testing could support validation in a real-world implementation.

points.title: Scope Boundaries
points.text: Not completed: recommendations were not implemented, post-implementation results were not measured, and formal UAT and handover were not documented.
